items.title: Greg Thomas interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: I remember Muddy Waters said, “The blues got pregnant and the baby was rock and roll.”

ctx.x: Well absolutely. I mean that’s one of the things Ellington and so many others — you can play the blues all kind of which way. You can play it slow, you can play a stomp, fast blues, I mean all kind of different feeling and flavors and approaches is there with that fundamental blues. And then it connects — through like the pentatonic scale it connects to music around the world. So the blues is so fundamental to American music and like I say through the pentatonic scale it connects to music around the world. So…
I remember Muddy Waters said, “The blues got pregnant and the baby was rock and roll.”

Yeah. Right, right, right, right. Yeah. Well then if the blues was — in that anecdote or metaphor if the blues was a woman then the father would be R&B. Because rock comes out of R&B. Especially through the person of Louis Jordan, who was jazz, R&B, entertainer, he had that whole thing.
